terms.gloss: of the house and household; family, private
evidence: Cic. Fin. 2.77: aliam domesticam, aliam forēnsem
terms.comment: Of the house itself (vestis domestica, clothes for wearing at home), but far more often of the family and its affairs: rēs domesticae ac familiārēs against public business, a family grief, home training; as a noun, domesticī, the members of a household (Lewis & Short). Household animals are avēs domesticae, poultry (Col.; M-O s.v. types: chicken: fowl); for the other sense, “not foreign”, see domestic (of one’s own country).

terms.gloss: of the household or family; intimate, familiar
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.2: rēs domesticās ac familiārēs (Lewis & Short, s.v. domesticus)
terms.comment: Of the familia, the household with its slaves and property: rēs familiāris is one’s estate. More often of persons, “intimate, familiar”, and as a noun a close friend (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: cum extrā rem pūblicam in domesticā rē atque vītā sedeātur, ambulētur, in convīviō quoque familiārī discumbātur
phrases.english: when, away from public affairs, in home life and domestic matters, people sit, walk about, and recline at a family dinner

phrases.latin: imbūtus jam domesticā disciplīnā, refertus honestīs studiīs dēdūcēbātur ā patre vel ā propinquīs ad eum ōrātōrem, quī prīncipem in cīvitāte locum obtinēbat
phrases.english: already schooled at home and full of honourable studies, he was taken by his father or his relatives to the orator who held the first place in the city

sources: Lewis & Short: domesticus · Lewis & Short: familiaris
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. types: chicken: fowl.
